title: How Bicycle Gears Work in 60 Seconds 🚲⚙️ #shorts
description:
Bike gears trade speed for force. A big rear cog makes climbing easy, a small rear cog turns every pedal stroke into several wheel turns. The derailleur simply pushes the chain sideways from one cog to the next. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#bicycle #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: In top gear, one turn of the pedals can spin your back wheel *more than four times*.

steps.label: Chain
steps.text: Your pedals turn the front *chainring*. The chain carries that pull to a cog on the back wheel.

steps.label: Low gear
steps.text: On the *biggest* rear cog, the wheel turns slowly but pedaling feels easy. Perfect for hills.

steps.label: High gear
steps.text: On the *smallest* cog, each pedal stroke spins the wheel many times. Harder to push, but fast.

steps.label: Derailleur
steps.text: When you shift, the *derailleur* nudges the chain sideways onto the next cog, while a spring keeps it tight.

steps.label: Ratio
steps.text: Count the teeth. *50 teeth* in front and 11 in back means about four and a half wheel turns per pedal turn.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Big cog climbs, small cog *flies*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
